bill.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Small Business Administration relating to "Citizenship and Residency Requirements and Recission of Procedural Notice 5000-872050" and "Revised Applicant Ownership, Citizenship, and Residency Requirements for 7(a) and 504 Loans".
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.

classification.plainSummary: This joint resolution would overturn two Small Business Administration rules that changed citizenship and residency requirements for applicants seeking 7(a) and 504 small business loans. If passed, the resolution would nullify these SBA rules and prevent them from taking effect. The measure uses the Congressional Review Act, which allows Congress to disapprove recently issued federal regulations.

industries.rationale: The resolution affects SBA loan programs that are administered through participating lenders and involve loan guarantees that impact banking sector operations.
SBA 504 loans are commonly used for commercial real estate purchases and development, so changes to eligibility requirements affect this sector's access to financing.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.
Banking & Finance is also the top donor sector for 2 other members from MA. That points to the industry being big in the state, not to anything about this member.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
